distractorNotes: That is what the GABA type A group does, and the passage contrasts these three against that group.
Glycine receptors appear in the same paragraph, but they are enhanced by the other group of drugs.
Two pore domain potassium channels are attributed to the volatile agents, not to these three.
The passage never connects any drug to doing without a relaxant.

answer.text: block a glutamate receptor instead of strengthening inhibition
answer.line: Paragraph 7, sentence 4: these three leave GABA largely alone and block the NMDA glutamate receptor, cutting excitation instead.

steps: Find the three names together: paragraph 7, sentence 4.
Read what they share: they leave GABA largely alone and block the NMDA glutamate receptor, "cutting excitation rather than boosting inhibition".
Sort the rest by group. Three other choices belong to the other drugs in paragraph 7; no line makes the relaxant claim.

choices.text: block a glutamate receptor instead of strengthening inhibition
choices.note: Glutamate blocked, GABA left alone: excitation cut, not inhibition boosted.

choices.text: make each pulse of the brain's inhibition last longer than it should
choices.note: Longer inhibitory pulses belong to propofol, etomidate, the barbiturates and the ethers in sentence 2. These three leave GABA largely alone.

choices.text: act on the glycine receptors of the spinal cord
choices.note: Glycine receptors come up in sentence 3, enhanced too, which ties them to the GABA group, not to these three.

choices.text: open potassium channels that make a neuron harder to fire
choices.note: Sentence 5 gives the two pore domain potassium channels to the volatile agents, not to ketamine, nitrous oxide and xenon.

choices.text: are the only agents that can be used without a muscle relaxant
choices.note: No line links any drug to doing without a relaxant. Paragraph 9 even says nitrous oxide cannot carry an anaesthetic alone.
